messages:
Ben: hey team, ben here (first week). quick question about escalation & channel norms: if I'm blocked by an external vendor (or a security finding), where do I post vs who do I DM? also when should something move from a channel thread -> ticket -> incident? thanks!

marie: welcome! good q. short rules we use: vendor/blocking external -> post in your squad channel AND open a ticket in #help (so infra/product can triage); security findings -> DM security@redwood AND post a redacted note in #security with the severity and ask for triage.

onboard-bot: Welcome Ben! To finish setup: run `rwi-setup verify` and join these channels: #eng, #devex, your-squad. Reply "done" to mark as complete.

Ben: thanks. how do I decide channel thread -> ticket -> incident? e.g., flaky CI failing my PR vs prod 500s.

Kai: simple flow we follow: in a channel thread for clarifying/helping individual dev tasks (e.g., CI failure on a PR) -> keep in the channel and link the PR/CI log. If the problem blocks multiple people or affects prod -> open a ticket and escalate to #incidents and @oncall. Prod P0/P1 -> incident.

ops-lead: fyi, use the tags: [Help] for single-person/blocking, [Escalate] for team-level problems to be triaged, [Incident] to show it's already impacting users. If you open a ticket, paste the ticket link back into the thread so context is preserved.

Ben: got it. vendor delays are often slow replies. do we prefer async updates in the same thread or open a ticket and maintain status there?

marie: for vendor delays: open a ticket and set the priority to P2 (if not user-facing) or P1 if users are impacted. Put short async updates in the channel thread (1 line) like "update: vendor says ETA 48h" and link ticket. That keeps chat lightweight and tickets authoritative for tracking.

Ben: nice. security finding example: if I see an S3 bucket misconfig, should I DM security immediately or post in #security?

ops-lead: DM security@redwood immediately (do not post secrets). After they've acknowledged, post a redacted summary in #security so the team knows there's a triage. If it's publicly exploitable or live -> call pagers too (@oncall).

Ben: thanks. one more: meeting pings and calendar invites in channels are noisy. do we have a rule?

Kai: calendar invites should go in the relevant squad channel only (no cross-posting to #general). If it's optional and org-wide, schedule it and @mention relevant user groups 24h in advance. For last-minute meetups use @here but only during working hours.

marie: etiquette recaps: 1) use threads for follow-ups, 2) use reactions for ack, 3) tag tickets not people for tracking, 4) keep messages searchable (add PR/issue links), 5) prefix with [Help]/[Escalate]/[Incident].

pager-bot: New: Pager rule reminder: P0/P1 alerts will page @oncall immediately. Ensure you keep DND rules updated if you're oncall.

Ben: awesome, appreciate the clarity. I'll open a ticket for the vendor issue and keep short updates in-channel. also posting intro in #introductions now. :wave:
